meta.notes: Practical instruction that puts someone to work. Never a joke at the body. She names a friend before a form can categorise her. She wrote the note about the nails on the ward habit, and it is about what the hand held, not about Adela's body or history.

threads.topic: I heard you from the stairs.
threads.source: B11, 4.2. No visit starts earlier. She is already kneeling. The player is in the body of a stranger, kneeling at their own.

threads.topic: You wrote something down, that night.
threads.source: B11, 4.5. Eighteen days before anyone looks for a glove.

tv_y2.line: Not that. Off the line, that's wet. Inside. And tell Omar to stop looking at his breaker and come out here. Some six hours, in this. I'll tell him myself.

tv_y3.line: Some six hours. I've told you what to get.

tv_n1.line: Everything goes in the book. You chart it or it didn't happen, and then it happens to the next person. Why are you asking? You weren't on shift.

choices.label: The sheet says "nails torn." Is that all?

tv_n1s.line: If you've got something, say it. I'm on at seven and there's a man on my ward who's been dying since Tuesday with great consideration.

tv_n2.line: That's what he copied. Right hand. Three-ten by my watch. "White kid under the nails, shreds. Not hers." Her gloves were in her bag and they were cotton, for the plates. I wrote what she was holding, because nobody else was going to ask her. Now you've asked.

tv_n2s.line: Keep it dry if you take a copy. I need that book.

tv_n3.line: She let me sit in the shop with my shoes off on my one Sunday and she didn't ask how I was. That's as close as it gets, with me. What else?

tv_n4.line: He had the page in his hand. He wanted a time and an address. Nobody reads a nurse's chart until somebody's dead, and then it turns out they don't read it then.
